title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a compliance failure at the power layer of a data center build, not a failure of a model or a software system. Sixty-two natural gas generators were installed and run at the Vineland construction site without the permits New Jersey requires for installation or operation. The facility was already partly in use while that equipment was running, so the unpermitted plant was supporting live operations rather than sitting idle.

Catching it required a permit review before installation and an inspection at commissioning, and neither happened on the operator's side. The violation surfaced when state inspectors visited in late July, which means detection came from outside the company. The same site had already drawn violation orders from the Cumberland County Health Department over excessive noise, so the compliance problems were not confined to air permits.

What is not established is whether the operator intended to operate without permits, and the homeowners' noise suit is an allegation that has not been decided. The reporting does not say what workloads the campus runs or whether any of them are AI systems.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at its Vineland data center construction site in late July. Each generator was 2,000 kilowatts, and none had required permits to be installed or operated. Officials said it was the largest fine ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey, for violating the Air Pollution Control Act.

The Vineland campus is planned as a 2.6 million square foot complex needing 350 megawatts, enough for a medium size city, and is slated for completion at the end of the year. Some of it is already in use. Homeowners have sued DataOne over noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department issued violation orders for excessive noise.
